summary.headline: Afcons Q1 FY27 revenue fell 20% to INR2,727 crore and PAT to INR30 crore; management expects H2-weighted recovery with no formal guidance.
summary.overview: Total income fell 20.3% YoY to INR2,727 crore (incl. INR56 crore other income) and EBITDA dropped 41% to INR263 crore at a 9.6% margin, while PAT fell to INR30 crore from INR137 crore. Management attributed the weakness to weather, slow land handover, labour shortages, pending clearances, stretched client payments (notably UP Jal Jeevan Mission) and lower turnover that left overheads uncovered. Order inflow was strong at INR13,219 crore, lifting order book to INR43,290 crore, while working capital and debt rose. Management declined to give revenue or profit guidance, pointing to Q3 and Q4 for a pickup.

segments.commentary: Urban infrastructure ~34%, marine ~32%, hydro and underground (incl. water) ~20%, surface (road and rail) ~14% of the INR1.5 lakh crore pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow guidance of INR30,000 crore reiterated; INR15,700 crore booked to date, and management says it is very confident of at least INR30,000 crore.
No top-line or profitability guidance given; management said it does not make sense at this point.
Management expects H2 to be about 55-60% of annual performance, with Q3 and Q4 recovering to earlier levels and a strong FY28 and FY29.
FY27 capex expected at INR700-800 crore; FY28 capex INR600-650 crore.
FY27 debt expected to close around INR3,500 crore; net debt around INR2,700-2,800 crore; management indicated a 5-10% improvement in working capital.
FY27 other income expected around INR400 crore; interest cost expected to fall as collections improve.
HSR C2 tunneling turnover to start from November; force majeure settlement expected in the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Two TBMs on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad HSR C2 package began initial tunnelling drives as scheduled; main tunnelling drives expected in the coming months.
TBM depreciation is charged per Companies Act rates; accelerated depreciation returns once TBMs are capitalised.
Strategic equipment base about INR4,300 crore, retained for marine and overseas projects where rentals are costly.
Capex of about INR150 crore capitalised in Q1; around INR700-800 crore planned for FY27 incl. payments for CWIP.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of INR13,219 crore in Q1; order book INR43,290 crore at quarter end; no L1 orders pending conversion.
Bid pipeline ~INR1.5 lakh crore for the remaining 9 months of FY27 and ~INR3.96 lakh crore over the next 2 years.
Large orders: Croatia railway (largest single order ever), Vadhvan Port breakwater (work minimal in FY27 due to approach-road and reclamation delays).
About 11% of order book is slow-moving or other (Bangladesh ~2%, JJM ~3%, slow-moving ~5.65%) and ~20% is in initial phase.
JJM order book INR1,221 crore (UP INR510 crore, MP INR414 crore, Rajasthan INR297 crore); UP receivable of ~INR400 crore largely unpaid.
Working capital elevated with uncertified work done rising; Q1 cash flow from operations negative, as is typical for Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there concrete evidence that execution is picking up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said symptoms are visible; Maharashtra government is resolving land issues, and an MP compensation issue is near resolution. Q3 and Q4 are expected to show a significant uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for Croatia, Vadhvan and HSR and HSR payments?
qa_highlights.answer: Croatia sees minimal spend in FY27 and picks up in FY28; Vadhvan is limited to geotechnical and design work this year. HSR past billing has been paid regularly and tunnelling turnover begins from November.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year revenue and H2 growth trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on Q2 or full-year revenue. It said H1 typically contributes 40-45% and H2 55-60% of annual revenue, and expects a similar split this year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt, working capital days and balance sheet numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management withheld absolute gross debt and working capital numbers because they are unaudited; it said working capital days rose marginally from March and pointed to net debt-to-equity of about 0.68x.

qa_highlights.question: Asset-light model versus owning equipment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it invests only in strategic equipment; overseas rentals are costly, equipment is paid back in about 9 months in Africa versus 48-60 months in India, and marine fleet is strategic.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow upside beyond INR30,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will first achieve INR30,000 crore and will update guidance later; INR16,000 crore has been booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and net debt targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects debt to close around INR3,500 crore, flat-to-slightly-lower versus March 2026, and net debt around INR2,700-2,800 crore, while spending INR700-800 crore on capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax rate rise to around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower standalone profit combined with losses in closed-project JVs and subsidiaries (ECL provisions and admin costs) and turnover-based tax in Bangladesh pushed the effective rate up; the tax amount involved was only about INR4-5 crore.

risks_watch: Collections and liquidity remain tight; UP JJM receivables largely unpaid and clients stretching payments across the board.
Working capital and uncertified work done rising; debt higher than March, with no audited figures disclosed until H1 results in September.
Execution depends on land handover, clearances and labour; Vadhvan and parts of Maharashtra projects remain delayed.
Interest costs elevated by interest-bearing client advances (38% of advances) and higher average borrowings.
Depreciation to rise in H2 as TBMs are capitalised; management would not give a FY27 depreciation figure.
Other income fell sharply from about INR450-470 crore in earlier years to an expected ~INR400 crore for FY27 and only INR57 crore in Q1.
key_quotes: Liquidity conditions remained tight and collections continued to be moderate during the quarter.

At this stage, we are definitely seeing the symptoms of it all happening, and some of the issues with respect to land-related issues are getting addressed by proactive activities undertaken by Maharashtra government.
Q3 and Q4, we believe, would see significant uptick.
Yes, INR30,000 crores, we are very confident of booking at a minimum.
So, in Q1, we are we are having overseas revenue around 16% from overseas market, domestic is 84%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and order wins (Q3/Q4 uptick, strong FY28-FY29) but cautious and evasive on near-term numbers: management declined to guide on Q2 or full-year revenue/profit, withheld gross debt, cash and working capital figures as unaudited, and deferred FY27 depreciation and ROCE/ROE. Liquidity and collections were openly described as tight.
